headline: He built roads to end traffic. Traffic won.

portrait.alt: Robert Moses in a double-breasted suit, pointing at a model of a proposed bridge
portrait.credit: Robert Moses with a Battery Bridge model, 1939. C.M. Stieglitz, World-Telegram. Library of Congress. Public domain.

slides.label: The bright idea
slides.title: A city out of room
slides.text: In 1930 New York's streets were jammed and its parks were few. **Robert Moses set out to fix both at once.**
slides.alt: Aerial view of cars streaming along the Grand Central Parkway through a looping interchange among houses and fields
slides.credit: Grand Central Parkway at the Kew Gardens Interchange, Queens, about 1946. U.S. Department of State. National Archives. Public domain.

slides.label: It worked
slides.title: Beaches for everyone
slides.text: Jones Beach drew 350,000 people in its first month. **Playgrounds went from 119 to 777.** His parkways carried families out of the city.
slides.alt: Aerial view of Jones Beach in 1936: wide sand, the boardwalk, bathhouses, the water tower and vast parking fields
slides.credit: Jones Beach from the air, 1936. U.S. Army. National Archives. Public domain.

slides.label: The backfire
slides.title: Then the roads filled up
slides.statLabel: people lost their homes to his highways, by Robert Caro's count
slides.text: And every new highway drew more cars. **The traffic came back, bigger.**
slides.alt: Traffic on the Cross Bronx Expressway in 1973, sunk below overpasses and ramps crowded with cars
slides.credit: Cross Bronx Expressway, 1973. Dan McCoy, EPA Documerica. National Archives. Public domain.

slides.label: Could anyone have seen it coming?
slides.title: Yes, and people said so
slides.text: In 1930 a transit executive warned that wider streets simply produce more traffic. **Moses's own parkways jammed soon after they opened.**

slides.label: The long cleanup
slides.title: Still paying for the Cross Bronx
slides.text: In 2024 the federal government put $150 million toward easing the Cross Bronx's harm to its neighbors. **Fifty years on, the bill is still arriving.**

slides.label: The ledger
slides.title: Worth it?
gains: 416 miles of parkway, by one count
costs: Parkways that jammed soon after opening
slides.text: He gave New York 777 playgrounds and miles of beaches. **It cost 250,000 people their homes.**

slides.label: Pattern
slides.title: Great for one, bad for all
slides.text: A faster road makes driving easier for each driver. So more people drive, **until it is slow again.**

slides.label: Lesson
slides.title: Make driving easier, get more driving
slides.text: Traffic is thousands of choices. **Make driving easier, get more driving.**
